idiom_name: expression-body function; interface delegation with by
implementation_notes: Kotlin gives the one-liner a compact expression form - fun cancelOrder(id: OrderId): CancelResult = repo.cancel(id) - and replaces whole blocks of forwarding methods with class OrderService(repo: OrderRepository) : OrderRepository by repo, where the compiler generates every interface method that forwards to the delegate; the spec shows the generated bodies as ordinary overrides. What by cannot do is rename an individual member, and a member overridden in the delegating class is never seen by the delegate's own methods, so the hand-written one-liner remains the tool for intention-revealing names and for the one or two members that must differ from the delegate.
pitfalls: by-delegation republishes the delegate's members and cannot rename them; adding an override changes what callers of the class see but not what the delegate's own methods call (they keep calling their own implementation).
The delegate expression is evaluated exactly once at construction: reassigning the backing property afterwards does not rewire the delegated interface.
Members win over extensions, so an extension function that appears to add a delegating name is silently shadowed if the class already has a member with that name.
